core_problem_solved: To provide a modern, feature-rich, and highly extensible HTTP client library for Java, enabling robust communication with web services and servers.
key_features: A rich and highly configurable API for building and executing HTTP requests
Advanced connection management and connection pooling for high performance
Support for various authentication schemes (Basic, Digest, NTLM, etc.) and cookie management
A modular architecture with support for extensions
era_and_niche: A leading, modern HTTP client in the Java enterprise ecosystem. It is the official, ground-up rewrite and successor to the original, obsolete `commons-httpclient:commons-httpclient`.
reason_for_obsolescence: This library is **not obsolete** and is actively maintained. It is one of the three major choices for HTTP clients in modern Java, alongside **OkHttp** (`com.squareup.okhttp3:okhttp`) and the native **Java 11+ `HttpClient`**. The native client is often preferred for new projects to reduce external dependencies if its feature set is sufficient.
